c.tagline: Emilia-Romagna's capital of Parmesan, prosciutto, and Verdi opera.

taxi.fareNote: Metered white taxis wait at ranks (the station and Piazza Garibaldi) or are booked by phone/app rather than hailed on the street; Uber is effectively unavailable, so use a licensed taxi or the local ranks.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance; 113 reaches state police and 118 reaches medical emergencies directly.

avoid.reason: The area around the train station can feel sketchy late at night; keep usual awareness there.

hood_desc: The compact medieval heart around Piazza Garibaldi, the Romanesque Cathedral and pink-marble Baptistery, Teatro Regio, and the vast Palazzo della Pilotta; best for first-timers who want the sights, food halls, and elegant streets all on foot.

The lively quarter 'across the stream' (the Parma torrent), traditionally the artisan and working-class side, now full of aperitivo bars, trattorias, and students, with the leafy Parco Ducale on its edge; suits travellers after local nightlife and character.

A practical, multicultural residential district just north of the historic core around the railway station; convenient for arrivals and budget stays, with everyday shops and eateries rather than monuments.

A green, calm area southeast of the centre named for the star-shaped Farnese fortress (the Cittadella), now a public park with jogging paths; good for families and travellers wanting quiet and open space.
A relaxed southern residential neighbourhood of parks, sports grounds, and local trattorias away from the tourist core; suits budget-minded and longer-stay visitors after an everyday Parma feel.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.pay: Buy tickets from tabaccherie, machines, the Roger app, or on board (small surcharge); a single urban ticket is about €1.50, with day passes available. Validate/stamp your ticket on boarding.
transit.hours: TEP city buses run roughly 5:30am to 9pm, with a few limited evening lines; taxis, cycling, and walking fill the late-night gap.
transit.note: Compact and famously bike-friendly, Parma has no metro or tram - TEP buses plus the flat, walkable historic centre and shared bikes cover almost everything.

bus: Piazzale Carlo Alberto dalla Chiesa (coach & Flixbus stops)

transit.m: TEP city bus to Parma centre (~15 min)
Taxi to the historic centre (10-15 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a cover charge (coperto) is often already on the bill, so rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is appreciated but not expected.
